Paragraph: Summary of Passage: Every individual acts according to their inherent nature and deep-seated conditioning. Even learned individuals behave in alignment with their psychological tendencies, making artificial repression ineffective and futile.
Situation/Problem_Faced: The futility and harm of forcefully repressing one's natural psychological and physical inclinations instead of channeling them properly.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Krishna points out that everyone acts according to their innate nature (prakrtim yanti bhutani). He directly asks, 'What can repression accomplish?' (nigrahah kim karisyati), urging authentic self-awareness over artificial suppression.
Outcome/Resolution: Arjuna understands that spiritual growth requires channeling one's natural makeup rather than suppressing it.

Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Futility of Repression: Understanding that suppressing emotions or nature only causes internal stress
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Self-Acceptance: Acknowledging one's current mental and physical disposition realistically
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Working with Conditioning: Directing inherent traits toward positive outlets rather than fighting them

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Sadrsham ceshtate svasyah prakrter (Acting in accordance with one's own nature)
Nigrahah kim karisyati (What can forceful repression accomplish?)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: All beings act according to the modes of nature they have acquired. Even wise people exhibit their innate nature. Forceful physical repression without inner purification is ineffective; one must instead regulate and elevate their nature.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: Repressing core emotions or suppressing your true psychological tendencies leads to burnout and neurosis. True psychological health comes from acknowledging your natural tendencies and constructively channeling them.
